---
title: "Metric overview"
description: "Choose a metric from the relationship your embedding should preserve."
---

An embedding can put the right digit next to yours and still put two whole groups much too far
apart. Which of those would matter for the way you intend to use the map?

## Choosing a Starting Metric

| What do you want to know? | Where to start |
|---|---|
| Who stayed nearby? | `nn_preservation()` counts how many of the original neighbors each point keeps. |
| Do dense regions stay dense? | `local_radius_correlation()` checks whether points with small neighborhood radii in the input still have small radii on the map. |
| Do distances keep their order? | `random_triplet_accuracy()` takes a point and two others. How often does the closer one stay closer? |
| Can I retrieve a label? | `roc_auc()` and `pr_auc()` tell you how well images of the same digit, for example, rank ahead of the other digits. |
| Did a patch change shape? | `local_procrustes()` aligns the same points in both spaces. See what happened to [one patch of the Swiss roll](reference-geometry.html#compare-local-shape-after-alignment). |
| Did a gap open up? | `gap_index()` compares triangle areas. See the [gap between three digits](mnist-pca-umap.html#inspect-the-gaps-between-digits). |
| Can I trust an island? | `steadiness_cohesiveness()` checks groups [in both directions](mnist-pca-umap.html#check-groups-without-digit-labels), without using the digit labels. |
| Did two classes become easier to tell apart? | Compare `class_pair_auc()` with the fraction of points closer to their own class centroid. To check angular spread, look at [the 5s as seen from the 3s](mnist-pca-umap.html#compare-angular-spread-from-each-digit). |

## Which metrics work on large datasets?

Around **5,000 observations**, check the memory budget before constructing a distance matrix.
One dense `N` by `N` double matrix takes `8 * N^2` bytes for its entries. At 5,000 rows, budget
191 MiB for one space, 381.5 MiB for a reference and one embedding, or 572 MiB for a reference
and two embeddings. A single matrix grows from 7.6 MiB at 1,000 rows to 763 MiB at 10,000 and
26.8 GiB at 60,000. Allow additional memory for coordinates, copies and working storage. The
practical limit depends on which metric you run and how much memory is available.

- **Distances and their ordering.** Use the full coordinates and reuse a sample of pairs across
  embeddings for correlation, EMD, stress or a distance-band profile. Check how many pairs reach
  the narrowest band. For `random_triplet_accuracy()`, the sample size is *per observation*.
  [Global distance metrics](#global-distance-preservation)
- **Neighbors.** A graph with `k` neighbors per row stores `N * k` indices. Keep the graphs from
  `nn_preservation(..., ret_extra = TRUE)` for overlap, local radii (which also need distances)
  and reciprocal neighbors. Brute-force search still compares every pair. For approximate search,
  [spot-check a few queries](mnist-pca-umap.html#spot-check-the-pixel-neighbor-search).
- **Exact ranks.** With Euclidean coordinates, `exact_rank_profiles()` can score a sample of
  queries against every candidate. It needs only one query's ranks at a time, but scoring *all*
  queries still requires quadratic distance work.
  [Try a query sample](#sample-queries-when-the-full-neighbor-pool-matters).
- **Class geometry.** `label_trustworthiness_continuity()` checks nearest-centroid consistency for
  every pair of classes. `class_angular_distortion_index()` estimates angular distortion from
  sampled triplets. Here `n_triplets` is the *total* number to draw. Both work on coordinates.
- **Patches and gaps.** Reuse a reference graph for `local_procrustes()` and fit one small
  alignment per point. For `gap_index()`, only the edges of the 2D triangulation need distances.
- **Shared neighbors.** `neighbor_dissimilarity()` starts with sparse graphs. One popular neighbor
  can occur in many lists, and every pair of those lists shares that neighbor. Even the scalar
  score can then require space for nearly every pair of observations.

**When to use a smaller dataset.** `nbr_pres()`, `trustworthiness()`, `continuity()`, `rnx_auc()`,
`rnx_curve()`, `pointwise_rank_preservation()` and `pointwise_rnx()` each take **two dense distance
matrices**. `roc_auc()`, `pr_auc()` and `class_pair_auc()` take **one per space**. If you need AUC
for just two classes, select those classes before computing distances. If the full matrices exceed
your budget, use the same representative subset in every space and report the candidate pool size.

For `steadiness_cohesiveness()`, start with a representative subset. It takes coordinates, then
builds dense distance and similarity matrices and repeatedly clusters sampled groups.
[Jeon and colleagues introduced the measures](https://doi.org/10.1109/TVCG.2021.3114833).
Quadra follows [ZADU 0.5.4](https://github.com/hj-n/zadu) for shared-neighbor and map weights.
Asking for pointwise scores adds more square matrices. Fewer iterations save CPU while the dense
allocations remain. The MNIST workflow ran exact coordinate ranks for all 5,000 images and used
1,000 for the group comparison.
[MNIST group audit](mnist-pca-umap.html#check-groups-without-digit-labels)

### Sample queries when the full neighbor pool matters

To estimate rank preservation for the full dataset, sample the **queries** and keep every row of
the reference and embeddings. With `x` and `maps` from the MNIST workflow, these 500 queries each
rank the other 4,999 images. The mean gives each sampled query equal weight.

```{r overview-sample-queries, eval=FALSE}
set.seed(42)
queries <- sample.int(nrow(x), 500)
profiles <- exact_rank_profiles(x, maps, k = 15, query_rows = queries)
vapply(profiles, function(p) mean(p$trustworthiness[, 1]), numeric(1))
```

Subsetting the coordinate matrices also removes candidates and changes what the ranks mean. On
the same MNIST queries at `k = 100`, 7s retained neighbors better than 0s in the 1,000-image pool,
while 0s did better in the 5,000-image pool. At `k = 500` in the larger pool, 7s led again. Report
the number of queries, the size of the candidate pool and `k`.
[Full-pool MNIST comparison](mnist-pca-umap.html#expand-the-candidate-pool-to-all-5000-images)

## Local Neighborhood Preservation

`nbr_pres()` compares neighborhoods from exact distance matrices.
`nn_preservation()` and `nbr_pres_knn()` compare nearest-neighbor graphs. All three count
the fraction of neighbors retained, as in [Chen and Buja](https://doi.org/10.1198/jasa.2009.0111).

`trustworthiness()` and `continuity()` score misplaced neighbors by their ranks.
`rnx_auc()` summarizes rank-based neighborhood agreement over many neighborhood sizes, while
`rnx_curve()` retains the individual scales. `pointwise_rnx()` gives the comparison per observation.
The rank penalties are from [Venna and Kaski](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-44668-0_68).
[Lee and colleagues](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neucom.2012.12.036) describe the RNX curve and
its [weighted summary](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neucom.2014.12.095).

To see how far the closest neighbors move in the ranking, use `exact_rank_profiles()` with
`mrre = TRUE`. A first neighbor that slips to fifth counts more than a tenth neighbor that slips
to fourteenth. You can follow the input neighbors into the embedding or trace the embedding's
neighbors back to the input.
[Lee and Verleysen's rank errors](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v4/lee08a.html)
[Worked example](local-preservation.html#can-the-same-neighbors-come-back-in-a-different-order)

See the [local preservation](local-preservation.html) article for examples and
related local diagnostics.

## Local Scale Preservation

Neighbor identity does not say whether dense and sparse regions keep their
relative scale. `local_radius_correlation()` compares the local radius around
each observation in the input data and output embedding, using either the
distance to the `k`th neighbor or the mean distance to the first `k` neighbors.
[Narayan, Berger and Cho](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-020-00801-7) use local radii to assess
density preservation in den-SNE and densMAP.

## Local Shape Preservation

`local_procrustes()` checks how much the same reference neighborhood changes shape after
rigid alignment. It can find distortions even when all members stay together. The matched patches
follow [Goldberg and Ritov](https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.2669). Quadra uses a fixed-scale residual.

## Regional Area Distortion

`gap_index()` locates expansion and compression in the empty triangles of a 2D embedding.
[Ros, Arleo and Paulovich introduced the index](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28324).
Their [implementation](https://codeberg.org/jros/gap-index) is available.
[MNIST example](mnist-pca-umap.html#inspect-the-gaps-between-digits)

## Local Graph Diagnostics

`mutual_neighbor_correlation()` compares the mutual-neighbor count pattern in
the input and output nearest-neighbor graphs. It asks whether points with many
or few reciprocal nearest-neighbor relationships in the input graph have
similar counts in the output graph.
The comparison draws on [drnb](https://github.com/jlmelville/drnb).

Use `neighbor_dissimilarity()` when the question is which pairs of observations gain or lose
shared neighbors. [Fujiwara and colleagues](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.13891) define the measure.
[Graph comparison](local-preservation.html#which-pairs-share-the-same-neighbors)

## Global Distance Preservation

`quadra` also contains random triplet and random pair distance methods for
global structure preservation:

* `random_triplet_accuracy()` checks whether sampled distance orderings are preserved, as in
  [Wang and colleagues](https://jmlr.org/papers/v22/20-1061.html).
* `random_pair_distance_correlation()` measures Pearson or Spearman correlation between sampled
  input and output distances. See [Becht and colleagues](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4314) and
  [drnb](https://github.com/jlmelville/drnb).
* `random_pair_distance_emd()` compares sampled distance distributions using Earth Mover's Distance,
  following [Heiser and Lau](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2020.107576) and their
  [code](https://github.com/KenLauLab/DR-structure-preservation).
* `random_pair_distance_stress()` compares matched sampled distances with a root mean squared
  difference. This comparison draws on [drnb](https://github.com/jlmelville/drnb).

For these metrics, `Xin` and `metric_in` define the reference geometry.

The [identity-permutation example](global-preservation.html#identical-scatterplots-different-point-identities)
shows which metrics notice when the same plotted positions belong to different observations.
Use [distance bands](distance-band-fidelity.html) to compare ordering and fitted-scale stress
from nearby input pairs through the entire pair sample. The rank and fitted-scale stress comparisons
follow [Takaeda's benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21779). Quadra samples pairs by default.

## Input and Ordering Conventions

Sampled pair and triplet metrics require dense, finite inputs; graph metrics
accept the sparse inputs supported by `rnndescent`.

`nbr_pres()` includes boundary ties, exact-rank metrics break ties by column
order, and supplied-graph metrics use their stored order.

Euclidean and squared Euclidean induce the same ordering but different
magnitudes. This distinction affects Pearson correlation, EMD, stress, and
local-scale summaries, but not neighbor, triplet, or Spearman ordering.

## Label Retrieval

`roc_auc()` and `pr_auc()` rank other observations by distance from each query
and treat matching labels as relevant. They require the
[PRROC package](https://cran.r-project.org/package=PRROC).

For each class pair, `label_trustworthiness_continuity()` asks how many observations fall closer
to their own class centroid and how that fraction changes in the embedding.
`class_angular_distortion_index()` measures changes in the angles that one class subtends from
points in another. These measures come from [Jeon and colleagues](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00278)
and [Gunaratne, Kobourov and Miller](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00637), respectively.
For the former, Quadra uses the unrescaled distance consistency of
[Sips and colleagues](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-8659.2009.01467.x).

See the [label retrieval](label-retrieval.html) article for examples and return
value details.
